summary: Remove a chosen set of characters from the beginning of a string.
documentation: With chars supplied, lstrip repeatedly removes leading characters that belong to that set, stopping at the first other character. It returns a string and leaves the rest of the text intact.
inputs: An object with text and chars strings, where chars is the set of removable characters.
returns: The text after removing its maximal leading run of characters in chars.
caution: chars is a set of individual characters, not a literal prefix. An empty chars string removes nothing; whitespace is not removed unless it is included in chars.
scenarios: Remove combinations of leading comment markers from imported notes.
Strip specified separator characters from the start of a code field.
Clean scanner prefixes made from a known set of padding symbols.
title: Strip marker characters, not a prefix
problem: Return text.lstrip(chars). Remove any sequence of leading characters present in chars. Preserve the trailing text and stop as soon as a character is outside that set.
hint: Pass chars explicitly so that default whitespace stripping is not used.
goal: Use str.lstrip() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
